config.title: Forms & Validation

intro.title: Forms & Validation
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a user registration form with real-time validation feedback that checks email format, password strength, and required fields. You'll learn how Angular's reactive forms work using FormBuilder and FormControl to manage form state and user input. The lesson covers implementing built-in validators like required and email, creating custom validators for complex rules, and displaying dynamic error messages that update as users type. You'll use Angular's FormGroup to organize form controls, subscribe to value changes for real-time validation, and apply conditional CSS classes to show validation states. By the end, you'll have a fully functional form that provides immediate user feedback and prevents invalid submissions.
intro.usecase: Forms and validation are fundamental to virtually every web application, from user registration and login screens to complex data entry forms in enterprise software. You'll find these patterns in e-commerce checkout flows, contact forms, survey builders, CRM systems, and admin dashboards where users input customer data or product information. Professional applications require robust client-side validation to provide immediate feedback, reduce server load, and improve user experience by catching errors before submission. Angular's reactive forms with built-in validators are essential for building scalable applications that handle user input reliably, whether it's a simple newsletter signup or a multi-step wizard for financial applications.

objectives: Implement reactive forms using Angular's FormBuilder service
Apply built-in validators to form controls for data validation
Configure custom validation logic for specific business requirements
Bind form controls to template elements using reactive form directives
Manipulate form state programmatically to handle user interactions
Integrate error messaging display based on validation states
Control form submission behavior with validation checks

steps.title: Import Angular Forms and Reactive Forms
steps.instruction: Import ReactiveFormsModule and FormBuilder from Angular forms
steps.hint: Import ReactiveFormsModule from '@angular/forms' and FormBuilder from '@angular/forms' at the top of your component file
steps.expectedOutcome: ReactiveFormsModule and FormBuilder are imported from @angular/forms
successCriteria: ReactiveFormsModule and FormBuilder are imported from '@angular/forms'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you have both ReactiveFormsModule and FormBuilder imported from '@angular/forms'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both ReactiveFormsModule and FormBuilder from '@angular/forms' to work with reactive forms.

steps.title: Create the registration form component
steps.instruction: Create an Angular component class named RegistrationFormComponent that implements OnInit
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator and export the class. Don't forget to implement the OnInit interface.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Angular forms modules here

// Create your RegistrationFormComponent class here
steps.expectedOutcome: A basic Angular component class structure is created with the name RegistrationFormComponent
successCriteria: RegistrationFormComponent class is created with @Component decorator and implements OnInit
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your component has the @Component decorator and implements the OnInit interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a component class with the @Component decorator. The class should be named RegistrationFormComponent and implement OnInit.

steps.title: Initialize FormBuilder in constructor
steps.instruction: Inject the FormBuilder service into the RegistrationFormComponent constructor using dependency injection
steps.hint: Use the constructor to inject FormBuilder as a private parameter. Angular will automatically provide the service instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: injecting a service in constructor
constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a constructor that injects FormBuilder service for creating reactive forms
successCriteria: FormBuilder is injected into the constructor as a private parameter
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure FormBuilder is injected as a private parameter in the constructor.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a constructor that takes FormBuilder as a private parameter. Use dependency injection syntax: constructor(private fb: FormBuilder) {}

steps.title: Create reactive form with form controls
steps.instruction: Inside the constructor, initialize the registrationForm property as a FormGroup with three FormControl fields: 'email', 'password', and 'name', each with empty string as initial value
steps.hint: Use this.fb.group() to create the form group, and pass an object with the three field names as keys and empty strings as values
steps.expectedOutcome: The registrationForm property will be initialized as a FormGroup containing three form controls for user registration data
successCriteria: registrationForm is created using FormBuilder with email, password, and name controls
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using this.fb.group() and including all three controls: email, password, and name.
steps.feedbackWrong: use this.fb.group() inside the constructor and create an object with email, password, and name as keys with empty string values.

steps.title: Add built-in validators to form controls
steps.instruction: Initialize the registrationForm by replacing the comment in the constructor with the FormBuilder group method, adding email, password, and name controls with appropriate validators
steps.hint: Use this.fb.group() to create the form with three controls. Add Validators.required to all fields, Validators.email to email, and Validators.minLength(6) to password.
steps.expectedOutcome: The registrationForm is initialized with three form controls (email, password, name) each having appropriate validation rules applied
successCriteria: The registrationForm is created using FormBuilder.group() with email, password, and name controls, where email has required and email validators, password has required and minLength validators, and name has required validator
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using this.fb.group() and that each control has the appropriate validators - email needs both required and email validators, password needs required and minLength(6), and name needs required.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form initialization needs to use FormBuilder's group method. Create three controls (email, password, name) with their respective validators using the Validators class.

steps.title: Create form submit handler method
steps.instruction: Define an onSubmit method inside the RegistrationFormComponent class that checks if the form is valid and logs the form data
steps.hint: Create a method that uses this.registrationForm.valid to check validation status and this.registrationForm.value to access form data
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an onSubmit method that validates the form and processes the data when valid
successCriteria: onSubmit method is defined that checks form validity and accesses form value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your method checks if the form is valid before accessing the form data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onSubmit method should check this.registrationForm.valid and use this.registrationForm.value to get the form data.

steps.title: Build form template structure
steps.instruction: Replace the placeholder template with a form element that uses the [formGroup] directive bound to registrationForm
steps.hint: Use Angular's reactive forms directive [formGroup] to bind the form element to your FormGroup instance
steps.expectedOutcome: A form element with [formGroup] directive that binds to the registrationForm FormGroup
successCriteria: Form element is created with [formGroup] directive bound to registrationForm
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using the [formGroup] directive and binding it to the correct FormGroup name (registrationForm).
steps.feedbackWrong: create a form element and use the [formGroup] directive to bind it to your registrationForm FormGroup instance.

steps.title: Bind form controls to input fields
steps.instruction: Replace the div element with a form element and add input fields with formControlName directives for email, password, and name
steps.hint: Use the <form> tag with [formGroup] binding and create <input> elements with formControlName attributes matching your form control names
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: binding form controls to inputs
<form [formGroup]="userForm">
  <input type="email" formControlName="email">
  <input type="password" formControlName="password">
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: A form element with three input fields bound to the reactive form controls using formControlName directives
successCriteria: Form element contains [formGroup] binding and three input fields with formControlName attributes for email, password, and name
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good progress! Make sure you have a form element with [formGroup] binding and input fields with formControlName attributes matching your form control names.
steps.feedbackWrong: replace the div with a form element that has [formGroup]="registrationForm" and add input fields with formControlName directives.

steps.title: Display validation error messages
steps.instruction: Add error message elements below each input field that conditionally display validation errors using Angular's form validation state checks.
steps.hint: Use *ngIf to show error messages only when a field is invalid and has been touched. Access validation errors through the form control's errors property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional error display
Please enter a valid email
steps.expectedOutcome: Error message elements are added below each input field that conditionally display appropriate validation error messages when fields are invalid and touched.
successCriteria: Error message elements with *ngIf directives are added for name, email, and password fields that check if the field is invalid and touched before displaying error text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure each input field has a corresponding error message element with proper *ngIf conditions checking both invalid and touched states.
steps.feedbackWrong: Not quite right. Add error message elements below each input that use *ngIf to check if the form control is invalid and touched before showing the error text.

steps.title: Add submit button with form validation check
steps.instruction: Update the existing submit button to be disabled when the form is invalid by binding the disabled property to the form's invalid state
steps.hint: Use property binding with [disabled] and check the registrationForm.invalid property to control when the button should be disabled
steps.analogousExample:
// Property binding to disable a button based on condition
<button [disabled]="someCondition">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The submit button is now properly bound to the form's validation state and will be disabled when the form contains invalid data
successCriteria: The submit button has [disabled] property binding that references registrationForm.invalid
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using property binding [disabled] and checking the form's invalid state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button needs property binding to disable it based on form validity. Use [disabled]="registrationForm.invalid" on the button element.

steps.title: Wire form submit event to handler
steps.instruction: The form already has the ngSubmit event binding to call the onSubmit handler. Verify that the form submit event is properly wired to trigger the onSubmit method when the form is submitted.
steps.hint: Check that the form element has (ngSubmit)="onSubmit()" attribute to handle form submission events.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: wiring a button click event
<button (click)="handleClick()">Click Me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The form submit event is properly connected to the onSubmit handler method through the ngSubmit directive.
successCriteria: The form element has (ngSubmit)="onSubmit()" event binding that connects form submission to the component's onSubmit method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: The ngSubmit binding is present but check that it correctly calls the onSubmit method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form needs an (ngSubmit) event binding to connect form submission to the onSubmit handler method.

steps.title: Test form validation and submission
steps.instruction: Test the registration form by trying to submit with empty fields,
steps.hint: Open the browser console to see the form submission output. Try leaving fields empty, entering an invalid email format, using a password shorter than 6 characters, then fill all fields correctly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form demonstrates complete validation functionality - submit button is disabled for invalid forms, and valid form data is logged to console when submitted.
successCriteria: Form validation prevents submission with empty or invalid fields, submit button is disabled when form is invalid, and valid form data is successfully submitted and logged to console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good progress! The form is mostly working, but double-check that all validation rules are functioning correctly for all fields.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form validation isn't working as expected. Make sure you test with different types of invalid data and verify the submit button behavior.
